papers.title: PD-1 inhibitor-associated Sicca syndrome mimicking Sjögren's disease successfully managed without immunotherapy withdrawal.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly associated with a broad spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including rheumatic manifestations. We report a case of ICI-associated sicca syndrome (ICI-S) mimicking Sjögren's disease, with a brief literature review. The patient was a 70-year-old man with BRAF-mutated metastatic melanoma who developed inflammatory arthralgias followed by parotid and submandibular enlargement, severe xerostomia, and xerophthalmia, during pembrolizumab therapy. Treatment was withheld and low-dose glucocorticoids (GC) initiated, with rapid improvement of joint symptoms and gland swelling, although marked xerostomia persisted. The diagnostic work-up revealed elevated inflammatory markers and positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), with negative anti-SSA/SSB. Salivary gland ultrasound showed grade 3 changes (OMERACT) and PET-CT confirmed bilateral sialadenitis. Minor salivary gland biopsy demonstrated T-cell-predominant lymphocytic infiltrate without CD20+ B cells, supporting an ICI-S rather than primary Sjögren's disease. Pembrolizumab rechallenge triggered a flare of sialadenitis and arthritis, controlled with GC reintroduction plus hydroxychloroquine and supportive measures. This case provides educational insights into the diagnostic differentiation between ICI-S and primary Sjögren's disease, supporting early recognition and appropriate management without compromising oncologic treatment.

papers.title: Synergistic antitumor effects of 5-fluorouracil and vorinostat in preclinical models of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic options for metastatic pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) are largely limited, highlighting the need for novel strategies. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and vorinostat (SAHA), alone or in combination in preclinical PPGL models. The growth inhibitory effects of 5-FU and SAHA were investigated in PC-12 cells and human PPGL primary cultures (n = 4) using CCK-8 assays. Drug interactions were evaluated utilizing the Chou-Talalay method. Specific mechanisms were explored via flow cytometry, wound healing, and transwell assays. In vivo efficacy and safety were assessed using mouse subcutaneous xenograft models. Both monotherapies inhibited PC-12 growth in a dose- and time-dependent manner (5-FU: 0-160 μM and SAHA: 0-80 μM). The combination therapy (20 μM 5-FU + 10 μM SAHA) exhibited a robust synergistic effect with the combination index < 1, achieving 43% growth inhibition in PC-12 cells and nearly 70% in primary cultures, significantly outperforming monotherapies. This combination significantly exacerbated G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and suppressed PC-12 cell migration and invasion. In vivo, the combined treatment reduced final tumor volumes by approximately 50% and significantly decreased the Ki-67 index. Despite mild body weight loss on days 15 and 21, no evident histopathological organ damage was observed. This study provides the first preclinical evidence that combining SAHA with 5-FU exerts a robust synergistic antitumor effect in PPGLs with no evident histopathological organ damage, laying a strong foundation for developing novel combination therapy for metastatic PPGLs.

papers.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with pancreatic cancer in high-risk patients under surveillance in CAPS and PCYST cohorts.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been linked with increased cancer incidence and mortality. We hypothesized that OSA may be a risk factor for neoplastic progression among patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surveillance. Retrospective medical record review of two Johns Hopkins Hospital cohorts undergoing pancreas surveillance; patients with familial/genetic risk enrolled in the Cancer of the Pancreas Screening (CAPS) study and patients with incidentally detected pancreatic cysts, enrolled in the PCYST study. Time-to-progression to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and neoplastic progression (either PDAC, high-grade dysplasia or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor) were compared by OSA status, adjusting for covariates. OSA was diagnosed prior to or during surveillance in 174 (19.5%) of 893 patients in CAPS and 376 (23.7%) of 1585 patients in the PCYST cohort. In the combined cohorts, OSA was associated with increased risk of progression to PDAC (unadjusted HR: 3.12, 95% CI: [1.82, 5.34], p < 0.001). OSA was also associated with male sex, higher BMI, fatty liver, fatty pancreas, diabetes, and history of smoking (all p < 0.01). After covariate adjustment, OSA remained associated with PDAC risk (adjusted HR: 2.56 [1.44, 4.55], p = 0.001). Factors associated with neoplastic progression included OSA (adjusted HR: 1.93 [1.25, 2.97], p = 0.003), increasing age (age-per 5-years adjusted HR: 1.14 [1.05, 1.24], p = 0.003), fatty liver (adjusted HR: 1.76 [1.19, 2.60], p = 0.005), and diabetes (adjusted HR: 1.77 [1.16, 2.71], p = 0.008). Patients undergoing pancreatic surveillance for their familial/genetic risk and/or incidentally detected pancreatic cysts have a greater likelihood of developing pancreatic cancer if they've been diagnosed with OSA.

papers.title: Crossing the Threshold to Emergency Surgery: Robot-Assisted Adrenalectomy for Refractory Pheochromocytoma Crisis.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma crisis can make conventional adrenergic preparation impossible and force consideration of adrenalectomy before physiologic recovery. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence that informs the transition from continued stabilization to nondeferrable tumor removal. Emergency presentation alone does not constitute an operative indication. When hemorrhage is controlled and cardiovascular and extracardiac organ function improved, surgery should be deferred until preparation is completed. Uncontrolled bleeding, expanding hematoma, or life-threatening compression requires immediate source-control assessment. Transcatheter arterial embolization may provide a bridge to elective adrenalectomy in selected hemorrhagic presentations. In nonhemorrhagic crisis, rescue adrenalectomy may be considered only when serial multidisciplinary reassessment shows persistent tumor-driven deterioration despite appropriate support, conventional preparation cannot be advanced safely, the lesion is localized and resectable, and organ injury remains potentially reversible. Mechanical circulatory support usually serves as a bridge to myocardial recovery and later surgery rather than as a routine platform for adrenalectomy. No validated temporal, hemodynamic, biochemical, or organ-failure threshold defines the point at which surgery becomes preferable to continued support. Operative access should therefore be selected only after the indication for surgery has been established and should reflect anatomy, physiologic tolerance, institutional expertise, and immediate conversion capability.

papers.title: Testosterone and DHEA-S Secreting Adrenal Cortical Adenoma in a Postmenopausal Woman: A Rare Functional Incidentaloma.
papers.abstract: Postmenopausal hyperandrogenism is uncommon and should prompt evaluation for an underlying androgen-secreting source. Although ovarian causes are more frequent, adrenal tumors remain an important consideration and may occasionally be malignant. We report a 53-year-old postmenopausal woman who presented with progressive hirsutism, scalp hair loss, and mild clitoromegaly. Laboratory evaluation showed markedly elevated total testosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate levels with suppressed gonadotropins. Pelvic ultrasonography showed no ovarian mass. CT demonstrated a 3.5 × 2.4 cm left adrenal mass with precontrast attenuation of 31 Hounsfield units and an enhancement washout pattern not typical of an adrenal adenoma. MRI showed a 3.6 × 2.1 cm left adrenal lesion with arterial hyperenhancement, restricted diffusion, and no signal drop on out-of-phase imaging. Biochemical testing excluded pheochromocytoma, primary aldosteronism, and clinically significant cortisol co-secretion. The patient underwent laparoscopic adrenalectomy, and pathology confirmed a 3.6 cm adrenal cortical adenoma with negative margins, positive inhibin, Melan-A, and steroidogenic factor-1 staining, and Ki-67 <3%. Postoperative androgen levels normalized, and adrenal insufficiency was excluded by cosyntropin stimulation testing. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical presentation, biochemical localization, adrenal imaging, differential diagnosis, and pathology when evaluating severe postmenopausal hyperandrogenism.

papers.title: Coexisting focal nodular hyperplasia and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal neuroendocrine tumor: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign liver lesion usually associated with vascular abnormalities. Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), on the other hand, frequently metastasize to the liver and typically appear as hypervascular lesions. The coexistence of FNH and diffuse hepatic metastases from an ileal NET is exceptionally rare and represents a major diagnostic challenge because both entities may present as hypervascular liver lesions, potentially leading to misdiagnosis and inappropriate management. A 56-year-old woman with a history of epilepsy treated with sodium valproate presented with progressive right upper quadrant pain and abdominal distension. Imaging showed a large hepatic lesion suggestive of FNH along with multiple hypervascular liver nodules suspicious for metastases. A CT-guided liver biopsy demonstrated metastatic well-differentiated NET with a Ki-67 index below 2%. Laboratory tests revealed elevated chromogranin A and urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid levels. The patient also had chronic diarrhea and moderate tricuspid regurgitation consistent with carcinoid syndrome. A ^68 Ga-DOTANOC positron emission tomography/computed tomography localized the primary tumor to the ileum. The integration of radiological, functional, and histopathological findings enabled accurate diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic planning. Surgical resection of the primary tumor was performed, followed by long-acting octreotide therapy. The patient remained clinically stable, with no progression of the hepatic lesions during follow-up. The presence of multiple hypervascular liver lesions in patients with NETs raises important diagnostic issues, especially when benign and malignant lesions coexist. This case demonstrates the value of integrating hepatobiliary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), histopathological confirmation, and functional imaging to accurately distinguish FNH from metastatic disease and to guide appropriate therapeutic management. The coexistence of FNH and diffuse liver metastases from an ileal NET is rare. This case highlights the pivotal role of a multimodal diagnostic approach combining hepatobiliary MRI, functional imaging, and targeted histopathological confirmation to distinguish benign from malignant hypervascular liver lesions, avoid diagnostic pitfalls, and optimize patient management.

papers.title: Mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma (MANEC) of the ampulla of Vater with sarcomatosis: a case report.
papers.abstract: Biliary mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are rare, accounting for only 4-24% of all intestinal MiNENs. Diagnosing them preoperatively remains challenging due to the limitations of biopsy and imaging. As a result, the optimal treatment strategy, particularly for postoperative management, is still poorly defined. A 61-year-old woman presented to the Surgical Department of Sfax General Hospital on 23 December 2021, with a 1-month history of jaundice, yellow discoloration of the eyes and urine, and clay-colored stools. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed dilated intra- and extrahepatic biliary ducts without evidence of stones or masses in the common bile duct. A positron emission tomography scan confirmed peritoneal and thoracic adenomegaly. The patient underwent a cephalic pancreatoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure). Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen confirmed a MiNEN. This case is particularly noteworthy for its rare association of a biliary MiNEN with a sarcomatoid component. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic complexities of biliary MiNENs. Given their rarity, sharing evidence-based clinical experiences is vital to standardize practices and improve patient outcomes. This report emphasizes the need for a multidisciplinary approach and thorough histopathological analysis to ensure accurate diagnosis and tailored management.

papers.title: Unicentric hyaline-vascular Castleman disease of the jejunal mesentery mimicking a gastrointestinal stromal tumor or neuroendocrine tumor: a case report.
papers.abstract: Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder classified as unicentric (UCD) or multicentric (MCD). The hyaline vascular variant of UCD most commonly arises in the mediastinum, whereas mesenteric involvement is exceedingly rare. As it can mimic hypervascular mesenteric tumors like neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) and gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. A 36-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of vague abdominal discomfort, early satiety, and an unintentional 9-kg weight loss. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a hypervascular jejunal mesenteric mass of size 2.0 × 1.7 cm, suspicious for a NET or GIST. Owing to the diagnostic uncertainty, exploratory laparoscopy converted to a mini-laparotomy with en bloc resection of the mesenteric mass and an adjacent 10-cm segment of jejunum was performed. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed hyaline vascular unicentric CD. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained asymptomatic with complete weight recovery and no evidence of recurrence at 12-month follow-up. Mesenteric unicentric CD is a rare but important differential diagnosis of solitary hypervascular intra-abdominal masses. As imaging findings often mimic mesenchymal and NETs, definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Complete surgical resection is both diagnostic and curative for localized disease.

papers.title: Non-ampullary duodenal mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasm initially diagnosed as adenocarcinoma: a case report.
papers.abstract: Mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are rare tumors composed of neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine components. Their occurrence in the duodenum is extremely uncommon. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the neuroendocrine component may not be detected in biopsy specimens. We report a rare case of non-ampullary duodenal MiNEN initially diagnosed as adenocarcinoma. A 56-year-old man was found to have a tumor in the duodenal bulb during routine endoscopic examination. Biopsy revealed moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, and computed tomography demonstrated bulky regional lymph node metastasis without distant disease. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with S-1 plus oxaliplatin was administered based on treatment strategies used for advanced gastric cancer in Japan. Post-treatment evaluation showed stable disease, and pancreaticoduodenectomy with regional lymph node dissection achieved R0 resection. Histopathological examination revealed both adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) components, leading to a diagnosis of MiNEN. Lymph node metastases demonstrated component-specific heterogeneity, with NEC involvement in station No. 8a and adenocarcinoma in the remaining metastatic nodes. Postoperative platinum-based chemotherapy was administered, and the patient remains recurrence-free at 16 months after surgery. Duodenal MiNEN presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because biopsy specimens may fail to detect the neuroendocrine component preoperatively. In the present case, component-specific lymph node metastases suggested biological heterogeneity and may have influenced treatment selection. Non-ampullary duodenal MiNEN is a rare and diagnostically challenging disease. This case highlights the importance of accurate pathological evaluation and multidisciplinary management.

papers.title: Primary large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the submandibular gland arising from a long-standing benign tumor: case report.
papers.abstract: Large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is an aggressive malignancy that commonly arises in the lungs. Primary salivary gland involvement is exceptional, presenting a major diagnostic challenge in differentiating it from metastatic pulmonary disease. A 62-year-old man presented with a right submandibular mass that had been stable for 16 years before rapidly expanding. Imaging revealed a massive 11 cm necrotic submandibular tumor with disseminated pulmonary and hepatic metastases. Following partial debulking, pathology revealed a high-grade neuroendocrine tumor (Ki-67 index 85%) arising alongside a benign mesenchymal component. Immunohistochemistry showed diffuse CD56 positivity and TTF-1 negativity. While histology mimics pulmonary variants, the dominant pre-existing cervical mass and chronologic evolution strongly suggest a primary salivary origin, likely representing malignant transformation of a benign lesion. This case highlights the rare phenomenon of primary salivary LCNEC developing within a long-standing benign mass. It underscores the importance of including high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma in the differential diagnosis of rapidly expanding salivary lesions.

papers.title: Proteomic profiling identifies candidate biomarkers for small intestinal neuroendocrine tumours G1 and G2.
papers.abstract: Although small intestinal neuroendocrine tumours (SI-NET) Grade 1 (G1) and 2 (G2) are often studied together, clinical course and response to treatment may differ. We hypothesized that these tumour groups express different markers in blood that may inform future treatment strategies. Blood from 107 SI-NET patients (G1 n = 64, G2 n = 43) and 50 healthy controls was analysed with proximity extension assay (Olink, Uppsala, Sweden). Two oncology protein panels were used. Outcomes were analysed with regression analysis and machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, Boruta). In age-adjusted analyses, 188 proteins differed between patients and healthy controls, with most being elevated in patients. Six proteins were elevated in G2 vs. G1 patients. After adjusting for age, Retbindin (RTBDN), Cryptic family protein 1 (CFC1), and Calbindin 1 (CALB1) remained significant, while adjusting for age and stage left only RTBDN significant. In a stage IV-restricted analysis, RTBDN was higher in G2 than in G1 (estimate 1.688; 95% CI 0.796-2.580; p <0.001). RTBDN and Midkine (MDK) were associated with poor survival, whereas the opposite was seen for Integrin subunit alpha V (ITGAV). RTBDN emerged as the only candidate biomarker associated with tumour grade after adjustment for age and stage in the G1/G2 analysis. In the stage IV-restricted analysis, RTBDN remained the top-ranked protein and showed a similar direction of association without reaching the strict Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. Higher RTBDN levels were also associated with increased mortality risk. These findings are exploratory and require independent validation before clinical application.

Non-Canonical Function of ORC1: Regulating Notch-VEGFR2-Mediated Angiogenesis in Melanoma Progression.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer characterized by high metastatic potential and substantial genetic heterogeneity. Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous susceptibility loci, the functional roles of risk variants, most of which reside in non-coding regions, remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify genetic susceptibility genes involved in melanoma progression and investigate their non-canonical roles in the tumor microenvironment. GWAS summary statistics from the GWAS Catalog, FinnGen, and UK Biobank were integrated using MAGMA and FUSION to prioritize candidate genes, which were subsequently evaluated using TCGA-SKCM transcriptomic and survival data. ORC1 emerged as a key susceptibility gene that was significantly upregulated in metastatic melanoma and associated with poor overall survival. Bioinformatic analyses further showed that ORC1 expression was positively correlated with Notch signaling activity and alterations in the immune microenvironment. The functional effects of ORC1 were examined using in vitro co-culture systems in which human umbilical vein endothelial cells were exposed to melanoma-derived conditioned medium. ORC1 overexpression in melanoma cells promoted endothelial prol iferation, migration, tube formation, and vascular permeability in a paracrine manner. Dual-luciferase reporter assays, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting indicated that ORC1 was associated with enhanced NOTCH1 promoter-reporter activity, activation of Notch-related signaling, and induction of downstream angiogenic programs. In xenograft models, ORC1 overexpression was associated with increased tumor growth and microvascular density, whereas pharmacological inhibition of Notch pathway activity with the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT attenuated ORC1-overexpression-associated tumor growth and vascular changes. Collectively, these findings identify a non-canonical pro-angiogenic role for ORC1 in melanoma progression that is mediated, at least in part, through Notch-VEGFR2 signaling. The ORC1-Notch-VEGFR2 axis may therefore represent a potential therapeutic target for modulating the melanoma microenvironment and limiting disease progression.

papers.title: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) promotes tumour cell growth directly or indirectly by activating immune-suppressive cells. In contrast to previous PI3Kδ inhibitors, roginolisib is a selective, non-ATP competitive inhibitor, which locks PI3Kδ into an inactive state and causes an allosteric modulation. In a First-in-Human dose study, continuous daily dosing of roginolisib was investigated in patients with solid and haematologic malignancies. In Part A, 24 patients received escalating doses of roginolisib. In Part B, 20 mostly pre-treated metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) patients received a dose associated with continuous PI3Kδ inhibition of >90%. The primary endpoint was safety, and secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) profile, clinical anti-tumour responses assessments. Exploratory endpoints included immunophenotyping, proteomics, genomics. No Dose Limiting Toxicity or drug related toxicities requiring dose modifications were observed ( ≥ Grade 3 toxicities: 3/44; 6.8%). In mUM, median Overall Survival (mOS) was 20.8 months (data-cut off December 2023) and 18.4 months (data-cut-off February 2026). mOS in mUM patients with Stable Disease at Week 16 ( = Cycle 5) was 28.5 months, while patients who progressed at Week 16 had a median OS of 12.3 months. Roginolisib was safe, had a predictable PK profile, T regulatory cell abundance was decreased while activated CD8+ T cells increased together with soluble plasma IL-15. ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT04328844.

papers.title: PET/MR Imaging of the Gastrointestinal Tract.
papers.abstract: PET/MR imaging combines molecular PET data with multiparametric MR imaging in a single reduced-radiation examination of the gastrointestinal tract. For oncologic indications, the hybrid modality adds value in hepatic metastasis detection, locoregional staging, and posttreatment response assessment. Radiotracers beyond fluorodeoxyglucose, including fibroblast activation protein inhibitor ligands and somatostatin receptor analogs, expand diagnostic reach in tumors with low glycolytic activity and in neuroendocrine disease. For inflammatory bowel disease, PET/MR enterography assists with selected questions such as differentiation of inflammatory from fibrotic strictures. This review evaluates current evidence supporting PET/MR imaging across oncologic and nononcologic gastrointestinal applications.

papers.title: Imaging Review of Small Bowel Pathologies (Benign and Malignant).
papers.abstract: Small bowel tumors are less common compared to large bowel tumors despite small bowel, being the largest segment of gastrointestinal tract. There is increase in incidence of small bowel cancers compared to large bowel cancer due to improved diagnostic imaging and endoscopic methods and increase in cross sectional imaging with contrast enhanced computed tomography. Diagnosis of small bowel tumors is delayed due to nonspecific clinical presentation and initial diagnosis is at advanced stage with local spread and distant metastases. There are several genetic and acquired predisposing risk factors for adenocarcinoma and lymphoma of small bowel.

papers.title: Imaging Review of Gastroduodenal Pathologies.
papers.abstract: The gastroduodenal region encompasses a complex anatomic area prone to diverse pathologies, including inflammatory, vascular, and neoplastic conditions. MR imaging is emerging as a useful diagnostic tool, providing superior soft-tissue contrast and high-resolution mural depiction without radiation exposure. Advanced sequences like diffusion-weighted imaging and dynamic contrast-enhanced MR imaging, combined with motion-compensation techniques, enhance tissue characterization and the accuracy of cancer staging. MR imaging is particularly useful for evaluating neoplasms. We discuss the practical uses of MR imaging in assessing gastroduodenal pathologies in this review article.

papers.title: Advancing Evidence Quality and Reproducibility in Endoscopic Endonasal Surgery for Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors: A Systematic Review and Reporting Guideline.
papers.abstract: Endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) is the primary approach for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNET); however, outcome reporting remains heterogeneous and inconsistent, limiting reproducibility, comparability, and evidence synthesis. We aimed to assess the reporting quality in EES-for-PitNET studies and develop a dedicated Reporting guideline. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to January 27, 2026. Original clinical studies (≥10 patients) reporting clinical, surgical, endocrinological, radiological, perioperative, or follow-up outcomes after endoscopic endonasal/transsphenoidal/transnasal surgery for PitNET were included. The reporting quality was assessed across nine domains: baseline characteristics, imaging and tumor features, definitions of key concepts, team characteristics, anesthetic protocol, surgical details, outcomes and adverse events, retreatment, and funding/conflicts of interest. Thirty study-records comprising approximately 15,800 patients were included. Reporting deficiencies were identified across all domains. Age (93%) and sex (100%) were almost universally reported and the treatment modality was always defined (100%); however, comorbidities were fully detailed in only 10%, and a comprehensive anesthetic protocol was essentially absent (3%). Key terms were defined in 53%, intraoperative adverse-event classification in 17%, and all-cause and procedure-related mortality criteria in 0%. Surgeon's experience was reported in 63%, time from symptom onset to treatment in 3%, and retreatment frequency and indications in 17% and 27%, respectively. Based on these gaps we developed the Endoscopic Endonasal Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor Reporting Guideline. EES-for-PitNET literature demonstrates substantial reporting deficiencies that limit evidence reliability and synthesis. The proposed Reporting Guideline provides a structured framework to improve transparency, reproducibility, and comparability in future studies.

Treatment profile and prognostic modeling in early-stage Merkel cell carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare but highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer. The prognostic associations of different treatment approaches remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to characterize treatment patterns, evaluate survival outcomes, and develop prognostic models for early-stage MCC. We analyzed SEER data from 2004 to 2021 for patients aged > = 20 years with node-negative, non-metastatic primary cutaneous MCC. Associations with overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were evaluated using Cox regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed for MCC-specific mortality in relation to adjuvant radiation therapy. Prognostic models were developed using Cox regression and XGBoost and evaluated using Harrell's C-index and time-dependent AUCs. Among 5742 patients, surgery was the predominant treatment modality. In direct comparisons among surgical approaches, gross excision showed only a modest and model-dependent association with OS and no consistent association with CSS relative to wide excision, whereas Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) was associated with higher hazards of all-cause and MCC-specific mortality. Adjuvant radiation therapy was associated with improved OS but not CSS. In the competing-risk analysis, the adjusted subdistribution hazard of MCC-specific death was modestly higher among patients receiving adjuvant radiation (sHR 1.17, 95% CI 1.02-1.34; P = 0.026). In the testing cohort, the Cox and XGBoost models achieved OS C-indices of 0.66 and 0.67, respectively. Treatment modality was associated with survival outcomes in early-stage MCC, although the observational treatment comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because of potential residual confounding. Cox and XGBoost models showed comparable prognostic discrimination in the testing cohort and may support further development of risk-stratification approaches.

papers.title: Distinct Molecular Pathways Driving Thymic and Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Organ of Origin Defines Molecular Identity and Yields CD44 as a Marker of Pulmonary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Thymic and pulmonary neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) are morphologically similar but arise from different embryonic tissues. Whether this similarity extends to shared molecular programs is unclear. We compared 45 thymic and 37 pulmonary NEN by immunohistochemistry, targeted and exome sequencing, NanoString RNA profiling and mass spectrometry-based proteomics. The RNA and proteomic profiles of pulmonary and thymic neuroendocrine tumors (LuNET and TNET) were clearly different, while the profiles of neuroendocrine carcinomas of both organs (LuNEC and TNEC) were largely overlapping. A subgroup of TNET corresponding to NET G3 clustered with lower-grade thymic NET rather than NEC. NET of both organs showed a low mutational burden and were proliferatively quiescent but diverged metabolically: LuNET showed broad metabolic and stress signaling and TNET a quiescent phenotype with PI3K/AKT/mTOR as the only enriched pathway. NEC of both organs converged on cell cycle activation and metabolic depletion with frequent TP53 and RB1 co-inactivation, but diverged immunologically: LuNEC were immune-hot, whereas TNEC showed epithelial-mesenchymal transition and a markedly lower mutational burden. CD44 stood out in both the transcriptomic and the proteomic analysis and was therefore immunohistochemically validated in an independent, larger cohort that included also gastrointestinal and pancreatic tumors. CD44 was high in pulmonary NET and low in every other subgroup (p = 2.1 × 10⁻¹³), identifying it as a new complementary marker of pulmonary origin. In summary, thoracic NEN segregate by anatomical origin as well as by differentiation grade. Wether these differences require treatments adapted to the organ of origin remains to be established.

papers.title: Wound Myiasis Complicating a Malignant Wound Caused by Merkel Cell Carcinoma of the Upper Lip: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Wound myiasis is a relatively rare condition characterized by the infestation of an open wound with fly larvae and may complicate malignant wounds associated with locally advanced cancers. We report a case of wound myiasis complicating a malignant wound caused by locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) of the upper lip. An octogenarian man with MCC of the left upper lip (cT2N1M0, Stage III) developed local recurrence after radiotherapy and was subsequently treated with avelumab followed by paclitaxel. Five days after the second cycle of paclitaxel, he presented with a chief complaint of tumor malodor. Physical examination revealed approximately 20 fly larvae within the ulcerated and necrotic tumor, leading to a diagnosis of wound myiasis. The patient was treated with saline irrigation and mechanical removal of the larvae and necrotic tissue. Thereafter, daily wound care was continued, and no recurrence of myiasis was observed. In this patient, advanced age, impaired physical function, and interruption of wound care because of pain were considered to have contributed to the development of wound myiasis. Because wound myiasis is a potentially preventable complication, appropriate pain control, continuous management of malignant wounds, and the establishment of a multidisciplinary support system involving family members and caregivers are essential in elderly patients with skin cancer.

papers.title: Case Report: Pituitary apoplexy temporally associated with acute alcohol intoxication, presenting as complete oculomotor nerve palsy in an SF-1 lineage gonadotroph PitNET.
papers.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy (PA) is an acute, potentially life-threatening neuroendocrine emergency caused by hemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland, most often arising in a previously unrecognized pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). Reported precipitants include surgery, anticoagulation, dynamic pituitary testing, hypertension, and head trauma; alcohol is rarely implicated. We report a 61-year-old man with long-standing hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease (on aspirin after coronary stenting) who developed sudden thunderclap headache and complete right oculomotor nerve palsy the morning after consuming approximately 250 ml of distilled liquor (baijiu). Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 2.7 cm × 1.9 cm × 1.9 cm sellar mass with heterogeneous hemorrhagic signal, suprasellar extension and optic chiasm contact. Perioperative endocrine evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism and low gonadotropins, consistent with multi-axis hypopituitarism. After aspirin withdrawal and immediate parenteral hydrocortisone, the patient underwent endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal resection on day 8. Histopathology confirmed an SF-1 lineage gonadotroph PitNET with extensive infarction (Ki-67 2%; FSH+, SF-1+, PIT-1-, T-PIT-). At 3 months, the right oculomotor palsy had partially recovered, with improvement in ptosis and ocular motility but incomplete resolution. Follow-up contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging showed no residual or recurrent tumor, a decompressed optic chiasm and a midline pituitary stalk, and the markedly elevated presenting 24h urinary free cortisol had returned to the laboratory reference range. Anterior pituitary function nonetheless remained deficient across the corticotroph, thyrotroph, and gonadotroph axes, and the patient continued stable hydrocortisone and levothyroxine replacement. This case adds to the limited literature on PA temporally associated with alcohol intake, illustrates the value of World Health Organization 2022 lineage-based PitNET classification, and supports individualized, semi-elective surgery in haemodynamically stable patients without acute visual-pathway compromise.

papers.title: [Clinicopathological and molecular characteristics of primary small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the breast: an analysis of nine cases].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinicopathological and molecular characteristics of primary small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (SCNEC) of the breast. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the 9 patients with SCNEC of the breast diagnosed at the Department of Pathology of the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, Suzhou, China from January 2011 to December 2025. Hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and next-generation sequencing (NGS) were employed to evaluate the clinicopathological characteristics, immunophenotypes, and molecular alterations. Treatment and follow-up data were also reviewed. Results: All 9 patients were female, with an age of 54.0 (45.0, 67.5) years. The maximum tumor diameter ranged from 1.8 to 10.6 cm. Pathological morphology exhibited features of small cell carcinoma. Necrosis was observed in 7 cases, intravascular tumor thrombus in 2 cases, and tumor involvement of the nipple epidermis in 1 case. All cases were positive for CKpan, chromongranin A and synaptophysin, while partial expression was noted for CD56 (7/9), ER (3/9), PR (1/9), TRPS1 (5/9), and GATA3 (3/9). All cases showed mutant-type p53 expression and loss of RB1 protein expression. The Ki-67 proliferation index ranged from 60% to 90%. NGS showed that TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene, with missense mutations identified in 3 of the 4 cases tested. Tumor mutational burden (TMB) analysis showed that all 4 cases had TMB <10 Muts/Mb, falling into the low TMB category. Microsatellite instability analysis revealed that 1 case was microsatellite instability-high, with a concurrent MSH6 frameshift mutation, indicating mismatch repair deficiency. Among the 7 patients who underwent surgery, 1 received neoadjuvant chemotherapy with marked tumor regression, and 4 received postoperative adjuvant therapy. The other 2 patients with advanced disease did not undergo surgery but received systemic chemotherapy after core needle biopsy. Follow-up data were available for 6 of the 9 patients, with follow-up periods ranging from 3 to 87 months. Three patients were alive, and three patients died at 22, 24, and 27 months after surgery, respectively. Conclusions: Primary SCNEC of the breast is a rare type of highly aggressive malignancy. Its diagnosis requires the exclusion of metastasis from other primary sites. The immunophenotype is mostly ER/PR-negative in this cohort, and GATA3 and TRPS1 are of limited value in confirming a mammary origin. p53 mutation and loss of RB1 expression are common molecular alterations in this tumor.

papers.title: [Controversies and advances in pathological diagnosis of breast neuroendocrine neoplasms].
papers.abstract: Breast neuroendocrine neoplasms represent a rare pathological entity. Iterative revisions of successive editions of the WHO classification criteria have resulted in poor interobserver consistency in pathological diagnosis. This review systematically sorts out the evolutionary trajectory of the histological subtyping of such neoplasms, comprehensively analyzes diagnostic challenges at the histological, immunohistochemical and molecular levels, and elaborates on the hierarchical diagnostic framework and differential diagnostic criteria proposed by the latest WHO classification. It aims to provide a theoretical reference for the pathological identification of this rare tumor, and facilitate standardized pathological evaluation as well as individualized precision diagnosis and treatment for mammary neuroendocrine neoplasms in clinical practice.

papers.title: Neuropeptides and their receptors in CNS cancer imaging/theranostics: Review of recent advances and increased interest with emphasis on the somatostatin/bombesin/substance P peptide receptor families.
papers.abstract: This paper includes a summary of the main points of our recent presentation at the 2025 RegPep meeting in Washington, DC. In the invitation to make this presentation by the meeting organizers, we were asked to include a discussion of peptide directed imaging and theranostics to areas that would be of interest to the attendees, which primarily includes studies related to the CNS. The interest in the possible application of peptide theranostics to oncology both generally and in the case of the CNS tumors has markedly increased over the last few years because of its successful application in both neuroendocrine tumors and prostate cancer, leading to FDA approved novel tumor approaches for both imaging these tumors as well as for its theranostic approach. In this paper we review the scientific basis for the successful application of peptide theranostics to neuroendocrine and prostate cancer, and the current status of its application to CNS tumors, particularly meningiomas, glioblastomas including glioblastoma multiforme, and medulloblastomas. We particularly concentrate on the possible use of the somatostatin, bombesin (Bn), and substance P (SP)/neurokinin (NK) family of receptors as targets, which have received the most attention and show the most promise in applying peptide receptor imaging/theranostics to CNS tumors. We also discuss the specific problems that the CNS presents in applying this approach to CNS tumors because of the blood-brain barrier in addition to the progress made. Clinical Trial Registry: NCT01578239 (NETTER-1)(NET), NCT03972488 (NETTER-2)(NET): VISION Trial (NCT03511664)[Lu-177-PSMA-617] (Pluvicto) in advanced prostate cancer.

papers.title: Clinicopathological Characteristics of Merkel Cell Carcinoma in Younger Patients: A Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma that predominantly affects older adults. MCC arising in younger patients is exceedingly rare, and its clinicopathologic features remain poorly described. We retrospectively reviewed clinical records, histopathology, and outcomes of patients aged 18 to 50 years diagnosed with MCC at a single tertiary care center between 2009 and 2025. A total of 13 patients were identified with a median age of 40 years (range: 18 to 50 y); 61.5% were female. Of 11 patients with available data, 36.4% had pre-existing immune suppression. Tumors arose most commonly on the extremities (46.2%), followed by the head and neck (23.1%), trunk (15.4%), and unknown primary (15.4%). The most common growth pattern was nodular (63.6%), followed by infiltrative (27.3%). Median Breslow depth was 10.5 mm and median mitotic rate was 46/mm². Immunohistochemical staining was consistent with MCC in all cases. Merkel cell polyomavirus was detected by large T antigen chromogenic in situ hybridization and/or immunohistochemistry in 62.5% of assessable cases (5/8). Lymph node metastases were present at presentation in 60.0% of patients, and distant metastases developed in 54.5%. Kaplan-Meier estimated overall survival was 74.1% at 2 years and 59.3% at 5 years. In this single-institution cohort, early-onset MCC was associated with elevated rates of immune suppression and a substantial burden of regional and distant metastatic disease, highlighting clinicopathologic distinctions from predominantly older historical MCC populations.

papers.title: Histiocytoid melanoma presenting as lymphadenopathy and mimicking Rosai-Dorfman disease.
papers.abstract: We report a case of a patient with large, unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. Excisional biopsy demonstrated expansion of the lymph node sinuses by a population of large histiocytoid cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm and large, eccentric nuclei with prominent central nucleoli. The findings were morphologically suspicious for Rosai-Dorfman disease; however, emperipolesis was conspicuously absent. Immunohistochemical work-up demonstrated that the infiltrate consisted of metastatic melanoma with histiocytoid morphology and admixed reactive sinus histiocytes.

papers.title: Impact of adjuvant therapy on melanoma-specific survival in elderly patients with high-risk resected melanoma: a multicenter international retrospective study.
papers.abstract: Adjuvant systemic therapy improves recurrence-free survival in resected high-risk melanoma, but elderly patients remain markedly under-represented in clinical trials; their competing risk of death from other causes needs to be considered. Consequently, the clinical benefit of adjuvant therapy in older populations remains uncertain. We conducted an international real-world study to evaluate survival outcomes of patients aged ≥75 years with resected stage III-IV melanoma managed with adjuvant systemic therapy or observation. In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, patients aged ≥75 years with completely resected stage III-IV cutaneous melanoma were identified across 14 international melanoma centers. Patients received either standard adjuvant systemic therapy (anti-programmed cell death protein 1 immunotherapy or BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy) or observation. The primary endpoint were melanoma-specific survival (MSS) and overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints included recurrence-free survival (RFS). Survival outcomes were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and evaluated with multivariable Cox regression models adjusted for age, stage, sex, and mutation status. A total of 580 patients were included (median age 79 years; range, 75-99), of whom 222 (38%) received adjuvant therapy and 358 (62%) underwent observation. Adjuvant therapy was associated with significantly improved MSS, with 5-year MSS of 74% compared with 60% in the observation group (adjusted HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.85; p=0.005), as well as OS (adjusted HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.87; p=0.002). Adjuvant therapy was also associated with improved RFS (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.72; p<0.0001). Among patients managed with observation, disease recurrence occurred in 69%, yet only 47% of those patients received systemic therapy as first-line management of recurrence. Notably, among observation patients who remained recurrence-free or received systemic therapy after recurrence, MSS was comparable to that observed in adjuvant-treated patients (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.55 to 1.25). In this large international real-world cohort of elderly patients with resected melanoma, adjuvant therapy was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in MSS, OS and RFS. Although immunotherapy retained efficacy when administered at recurrence, many elderly patients did not receive systemic therapy as first-line management of recurrence. Adjuvant therapy may therefore represent an important strategy to ensure timely access to effective treatment in carefully selected older patients.

papers.title: Risk of abnormal histology following vaginal hysterectomy for pelvic organ prolapse in a multi-ethnic Asian population: a two-year retrospective review.
papers.abstract: Vaginal hysterectomy is frequently performed for benign conditions like pelvic organ prolapse. While pre-operative screening is intended to pick up malignancies in advance, unexpected findings of abnormal histology can still arise post-operatively. This study aims to determine the prevalence of unanticipated gynaecological malignancy and pre-malignancy in women who underwent vaginal hysterectomy for pelvic organ prolapse in a multi-ethnic Asian population. A retrospective audit of medical records of 512 women underwent vaginal hysterectomy with or without salpingo-oophorectomy for the treatment of pelvic organ prolapse between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024 at KK Women's and Children's Hospital, Singapore, was conducted. Patients with pre-operative diagnosis of gynaecological malignancy or pre-malignancy were excluded. Pre-operative demographic data, cytopathological and histopathological investigations, as well as post-operative histopathological results were reviewed. Abnormal histopathological findings were identified in 34 patients (6.6 %) post-operatively. Malignancy was diagnosed in 4 patients (0.8 %) while pre-malignant histology was found in 29 patients (5.7 %). Four patients (0.8 %) were diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma and 27 patients (5.3 %) were found to have endometrial hyperplasia. Two (0.4 %) patients had cervical intraepithelial neoplasia despite normal pre-operative cervical screening. Among the 88 patients who underwent concurrent salpingo-oophorectomy, 1 patient (1.1 %) was found to have carcinoid tumour of the ovary. Routine histopathological examination of hysterectomy specimens is essential. While the risk of unanticipated gynaecological malignancy is low, women undergoing prolapse surgery should be advised the risk of undetected concurrent malignant and pre-malignant gynaecological conditions.

papers.title: YTHDF2 drives malignant progression in cutaneous melanoma through m⁶A-dependent HMOX1-mediated ferroptosis.
papers.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification plays a critical role in eukaryotic mRNA and is significantly associated with cutaneous melanoma. This study investigated the role of the m6A-binding protein YTHDF2 in the pathogenesis of cutaneous melanoma and its potential therapeutic applications. Analyses of public databases indicated that YTHDF2 exhibited elevated expression in various cancers, including cutaneous melanoma, where its levels positively correlated with PD-L1 and negatively correlated with immune and stromal scores. Functionally, the downregulation of YTHDF2 in melanoma cells suppressed proliferation and increased the population of Annexin V/PI--positive cells, an effect that was rescued by the ferroptosis inhibitor, highlighting YTHDF2's involvement in ferroptosis regulation. YTHDF2 knockdown resulted in increased intracellular Fe2+ levels, malondialdehyde, reactive oxygen species, and lipid peroxidation, alongside a reduction in glutathione-effects that were reversed upon ferroptosis inhibition. In vivo studies corroborated the regulatory role of YTHDF2 in ferroptosis. Mechanistically, integrated RNA-seq and RIP-seq analyses demonstrated that YTHDF2 could bind to m6A on HMOX1 transcripts, destabilizing its mRNA and thus regulating HMOX1 expression. Moreover, metformin was shown to inhibit YTHDF2 expression, promoting ferroptosis in melanoma cells. In summary, YTHDF2 modulates ferroptosis in melanoma through the regulation of m6A-dependent HMOX1 mRNA stability, suggesting it as a promising therapeutic target. The capacity of metformin to suppress YTHDF2 indicates its potential utility in hindering melanoma progression.

papers.title: Applying 177Lu-Dotatate for Hereditary Neuroendocrine Tumours: The Role in MEN1.
papers.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) is the most common genetic syndrome causing neuroendocrine tumours (NET) with metastatic duodenopancreatic NET (dpNET) forming the predominant cause of MEN1-related mortality. Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with [177Lu]Lu-[DOTA0,Tyr3]-octreotate (177Lu-Dotatate) is an established treatment for advanced dpNET. As MEN1 loss-of-function has been associated with potential radiosensitising effects, this retrospective study evaluated outcomes of patients with germline MEN1-associated NET after treatment with 177Lu-Dotatate. This is a retrospective cohort study in patients with MEN1 and metastatic NET treated with 177Lu-Dotatate compared to a control group of patients with advanced sporadic pancreas NET (panNET). Survival outcomes, response rates and adverse events after the initiation of 177Lu-Dotatate were evaluated. A total of nineteen MEN1 patients with dpNET and fifty-seven sporadic panNET controls were included. No significant difference in median progression-free survival with 39.6 months (95%CI 13.7-65.5) in the MEN1 group versus 45.0 months (95%CI 35.7-54.3) in the control group was seen, with a hazard ratio of 1.086 (95%CI 0.60-1.98). Overall survival was similar between groups with 97.8 months (95%CI 36.3-159.3) and 89.3 months (95%CI 54.6-123.9), respectively, and a hazard ratio of 0.883 (95%CI 0.43-1.82). There were no significant differences in objective radiological response (44.4% in the MEN1 group versus 35.2% in the control group) or in grade ≥ 3 toxicity. MEN1 patients with advanced dpNET benefit equally from 177Lu-Dotatate treatment as those with sporadic panNET in terms of survival and response. These findings support the use of PRRT in MEN1-associated dpNET similar to sporadic cases.

papers.title: Rapid Native and Bioprosthetic Tricuspid Valve Degeneration in Carcinoid Heart Disease.
papers.abstract: Carcinoid heart disease (CaHD) is a severe complication of metastatic neuroendocrine tumors characterized by serotonin-mediated fibrotic degeneration of right-sided cardiac valves. We present 3 patients with metastatic neuroendocrine tumors complicated by severe carcinoid valvulopathy involving native and prosthetic tricuspid valves. Two patients underwent bioprosthetic tricuspid valve replacement for severe tricuspid regurgitation, including 1 patient who developed rapid recurrent prosthetic valve degeneration requiring transcatheter tricuspid valve-in-valve replacement. A third patient presented with advanced bivalvular carcinoid involvement requiring complex surgical reconstruction complicated by postoperative cardiogenic shock and death. These cases illustrate the progressive nature of serotonin-mediated valvular degeneration, challenges in prosthetic valve selection, and the importance of multidisciplinary management and close echocardiographic surveillance in CaHD. Persistent serotonin exposure may result in rapid degeneration of native and bioprosthetic valves despite surgical intervention. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are essential to optimize outcomes in CaHD.

papers.title: Psychosocial mediators for the impact of personal genomic risk information on melanoma prevention and early detection behaviors.
papers.abstract: In the Melanoma Genomics Managing Your Risk Study, receiving personal genomic risk testing led to improvements in some melanoma prevention and early detection behaviors. We aimed to examine the hypothesized psychosocial mediators of the effects observed in the trial. Australians of European ancestry without melanoma and aged 18-69 years were recruited via the national Medicare database and randomized to receive personal genomic risk information or usual care (N = 1025). Questionnaires were administered at baseline, 1-month post-intervention, and 12-months post-baseline to assess self-reported prevention and early detection behaviors and psychosocial measures. We first evaluated the intervention's effect on psychosocial measures and the associations between psychosocial measures and behavioral outcomes. We then estimated the natural indirect effects (NIEs) and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs) to quantify the effects mediated by potential mediators identified. Among participants with high traditional melanoma risk, the intervention's effect on increased sun protection at 1 month was partially mediated by changes in the perceived importance (NIE mean difference 0.02; 95% CI: 0.00-0.04) and perceived effectiveness (0.01; 0.00-0.03]) of sun protection strategies. Among women, the intervention's effect on increased whole-body skin examinations at 1 month was partially mediated by perceived capability to engage in skin examinations (NIE odds ratio 1.08; 95% CI: 1.00-1.29) and perceived control over detecting a future melanoma (1.13; 1.03-1.32). The effectiveness of precision prevention and early detection interventions may be enhanced by targeting key psychosocial mediators through tailored communication of personal melanoma risk.
