papers.title: Potential for pathogenic protein acylation in succinate dehydrogenase-deficient pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
papers.abstract: Historically, the study of cellular metabolism and the cellular proteome have largely focused on specific proteins and metabolites in certain cellular pathways. With the advent of new "omics" technologies, researchers have been able to probe disruptions and alterations in cellular homeostasis on a near proteome-wide and metabolome-wide basis. Yet the truly interconnected and interdependent nature of the cellular metabolome and proteome has only become more evident with the discovery of proteome-wide protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) such as lysine acylation by acetyl-CoA or succinyl-CoA. Such PTMs link proteome function to fluctuating concentrations of tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle metabolites. Tumorigenesis in TCA cycle-defective tumors that upregulate acylating agents such as succinyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA provides a relevant context for understanding the breadth of protein acylation in disease. In particular, succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-loss chromaffin cells can be transformed to the neuroendocrine tumors pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), but sensitive diagnostic and effective therapeutic options for metastatic disease remain limited. Interrogating cell models of SDH-loss PPGL provides a unique opportunity to capture the effects of SDH loss on cellular metabolism and protein acylation while exploring new avenues for improved diagnostics and novel therapeutic targets in these rare diseases.

papers.title: Effects of a GLP-1 agonist and anti-diabetic therapies on pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma growth.
papers.abstract: A high proportion of patients with pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) show glycemic dysregulation. However, studies on the effects of anti-diabetic drugs on PPGL tumor growth are still lacking. We evaluated the effects of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) semaglutide, metformin and insulin on fresh patient-derived PPGL primary cultures (n=54), including 8 cluster 1 tumors and 18 cluster 2/3 tumors (n=4 tumors with RET pathogenic variants [PVs]). We correlated the primary culture data with clinical data from 67 patients enrolled in the prospective clinical trial PROSPHEO (NCT03344016). We found cluster-dependent effects of semaglutide in patient primary cultures, with significant anti-tumor effects in cluster 1 PPGLs. Interestingly, we found tumor-promoting effects of high-dose semaglutide in 3 PPGLs with germline RET PVs (MEN2 syndrome), but not in a PPGL with a somatic RET PV. Metformin displayed overall anti-tumor effects while insulin showed individual tumor-promoting effects in the patient primary cultures. Consistently, clinical data confirmed larger median tumor sizes of PPGL patients receiving insulin therapy compared to patients receiving metformin/GLP-1RA therapy or patients without anti-diabetic therapy. Overall, we provide novel data on the effects of anti-diabetic drugs on PPGL tumor growth including significant anti-tumor effects of the GLP-1RA semaglutide in cluster 1 PPGLs, and tumor-promoting effects in patients with MEN2 syndrome. Further confirmation of our data in prospective clinical studies is required.

papers.title: Primary Intraosseous Cavernous Hemangioma of the Petrous Bone Involving the Jugular Fossa Mimicking a Jugular Paraganglioma: A Radiologic-Pathologic Correlation and Review of Relevant Literature.
papers.abstract: Primary intraosseous cavernous hemangioma (PICH) is a rare benign vascular tumor that predominantly involves the vertebral column and calvarium, while skull base involvement, particularly the jugular fossa, is exceptionally uncommon. We report a histopathologically confirmed PICH centered in the petrous temporal bone showing jugular fossa and jugular foraminal involvement, radiologically mimicking a jugular paraganglioma. A 46-year-old man presented with progressive unilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a heterogeneously enhancing jugular foramen lesion with cerebellopontine angle extension, whereas high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) revealed characteristic coarse trabecular ("honeycomb") architecture, smooth osseous expansion, and cortical remodeling, establishing its intraosseous origin and substantially narrowing the differential diagnosis. Histopathological examination confirmed cavernous hemangioma. This case highlights the complementary roles of CT and MRI in characterizing complex skull base lesions and demonstrates how recognition of characteristic osseous trabeculation, absence of aggressive bone destruction, and preservation of vascular patency despite encasement can differentiate PICH from jugular paraganglioma, schwannoma, meningioma, chordoma, chondrosarcoma, and metastatic disease. In conjunction with a review of the literature, this report expands the limited spectrum of jugular foramen PICH and underscores the importance of considering this rare entity in the differential diagnosis of destructive skull base lesions to facilitate accurate preoperative diagnosis and surgical planning.

papers.title: Surgical management of ectopic Cushing's syndrome from a pulmonary carcinoid secreting CRH supported by intraoperative ACTH monitoring - a case report.
papers.abstract: An intraoperative ACTH monitoring during resection of hormone-secreting neuroendocrine neoplasms remains a subject of a debate. We present the case of a 36-year-old man with clinical and biochemical features of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism. Dynamic endocrine testing, including the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, metyrapone test, and desmopressin stimulation test resulted in inconclusive results, precluding clear differentiation between Cushing's disease and ectopic Cushing's syndrome. Pituitary imaging revealed no definite focal lesion, whereas chest imaging detected a small pulmonary nodule along with an incidental adrenal adenoma. Taking into account rapid clinical course and the severity of clinical symptoms surgical resection of the lung lesion was undertaken with intraoperative ACTH monitoring. Due to compilation of factors patient was sent to thoracic surgery without delay. A transient ACTH surge was observed during first stage tumor excision and, even though intraoperative pathological and surgical findings indicated the complete tumor resection, which contributed to the decision to extend the procedure to an upper lobectomy, after which a marked and sustained decline in ACTH concentrations was observed. Histopathological examination confirmed a typical pulmonary carcinoid tumor, and surgical treatment resulted in clinical and biochemical remission, followed by gradual recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. This case highlights the limitations of dynamic testing and imaging in ECS, particularly in indolent presentation, and underscored the potential value of intraoperative ACTH monitoring as an adjunctive tool for tumor localization and surgical decision-making.

papers.title: Multi-sequence MRI signal intensity ratios as candidate imaging correlates for audiovestibular dysfunction in vestibular schwannoma.
papers.abstract: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) typically induces gradual sensorineural hearing impairment and vestibular dysfunction. Nevertheless, clinically applicable non-invasive candidate imaging markers capable of reflecting pathological alterations within the inner ear have not yet been well established. The present study sought to systematically investigate the correlative relationships between labyrinth signal intensity ratios acquired from multi-sequence inner ear magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and audiovestibular functional deficits in patients diagnosed with VS. A total of 22 patients with radiologically confirmed VS were consecutively enrolled for this retrospective observational study. All subjects received 3.0 T inner ear MRI examinations covering three pulse sequences: T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), pre-contrast three-dimensional fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (3D-FLAIR), and delayed post-contrast 3D-FLAIR acquired at the 4-h time point after gadolinium administration. Signal intensity ratios (cochlea-, vestibule-, and semicircular canal-to-brainstem; CBR, VBR, SBR) were measured and correlated with pure-tone audiometry, caloric testing, and video head impulse test (vHIT) results. Compared to contralateral unaffected ears, affected ears exhibited significantly elevated signal ratios on both delayed post-contrast and pre-contrast 3D-FLAIR sequences (all p < 0.001), indicating blood-labyrinth barrier disruption, while T2WI ratios were significantly reduced (p < 0.001), suggesting structural alterations like increased protein content. Correlation analysis revealed that pre-contrast 3D-FLAIR CBR exhibited a moderate positive correlation with the degree of hearing loss (r = 0.582, p = 0.037), whereas T2WI SBR showed a correlation with low-frequency vestibular dysfunction assessed by caloric testing (r = 0.440, p = 0.040). In contrast, none of the evaluated MRI metrics demonstrated significant correlations with high-frequency vestibular function measured by vHIT. These findings demonstrate that specific inner ear MRI signal ratios serve as promising candidate imaging correlates for auditory impairment and low-frequency vestibular deficits in VS. Pre-contrast 3D-FLAIR and T2WI sequences offer distinct insights into inflammatory leakage and structural damage, respectively. The potential for these metrics to guide personalized management strategies remains to be evaluated in future studies. Large-scale multicenter investigations incorporating histopathologic verification are therefore needed to dissect these underlying mechanisms and develop predictive prognostic frameworks.

papers.title: Clinical and imaging differentiation of intrapancreatic accessory spleen from pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor and solid-pseudopapillary tumor: a retrospective analysis.
papers.abstract: Intrapancreatic accessory spleen (IPAS) represents a rare anatomical variant of the spleen that is misdiagnosed as pancreatic neoplastic lesions. Notably, IPAS is often erroneously identified as pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PNET) or solid pseudopapillary tumor (SPT), which consequently results in unnecessary resection of the pancreas. This study aimed to summarize the clinical, imaging and laboratory characteristics of these lesions, clarify the key differential diagnostic points among them, and thereby enhance the clinical understanding and preoperative diagnostic accuracy of IPAS. This retrospective study analyzed all 7 cases of IPAS diagnosed at our hospital from January 2008 to December 2025. For comparative analysis, consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed PNET (n = 18) and SPT (n = 21) treated at the same institution between January 2023 and June 2025 were included. Clinical, imaging and pathologic characteristics were compared descriptively. Key points of differential diagnosis were summarized. IPAS was distinguished from PNET and SPT primarily by consistent location in the pancreatic tail (100%), frequent heterogeneous arterial-phase enhancement with CT attenuation often similar to the spleen, universal adjacency to the splenic vessels, solid consistency, and predominantly reddish-brown gross appearance, with most lesions showing a soft texture. In contrast, PNET and SPT showed more variable location, enhancement patterns, attenuation relative to spleen, vessel contact rates, and pathologic color/texture. SPTs are typically larger and more frequently exhibit calcification. For lesions located in the pancreatic tail, adjacent to the spleen, and exhibiting heterogeneous enhancement in the arterial phase, the possibility of IPAS should be thoroughly considered. Nevertheless, surgical resection remains rational and appropriate when preoperative evaluation cannot completely exclude the possibility of PNET, SPT, or other pancreatic lesions.

papers.title: A Novel Hybrid Endovascular Technique for Tympanojugular Paraganglioma: Flow Diversion Followed by Direct Transauricular Squid Embolization.
papers.abstract: Skull-base paragangliomas with persistent internal carotid artery (ICA) supply can be challenging to devascularize safely. We report a 17-yearold male with an Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Iron Sulfur Subunit B (SDHB)-associated tympanojugular paraganglioma treated using a staged hybrid endovascular strategy after subtotal resection. Persistent supply from a short ICA feeder and circumferential involvement of the petrous ICA precluded safe conventional transarterial embolization. A Surpass Elite flow-diverting stent was deployed across the feeder after dual antiplatelet therapy to preserve parent-vessel patency, reduce tumour inflow, and reinforce the arterial wall. Four months later, protected direct transauricular and transcervical puncture embolization with Squid 12 was performed under intermittent ICA balloon occlusion. Marked tumor devascularization was achieved without embolic or thromboembolic complication, and definitive resection was completed without new neurological or cranial nerve deficit. This staged approach may provide a useful adjunct for selected skull-base paragangliomas with persistent ICA supply when conventional embolization carries unacceptable risk.

papers.title: Perspectives on 10 years of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Podcast.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and aggressive skin cancer with a poor prognosis, particularly in patients with advanced disease. The introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) approximately 10 years ago has dramatically improved outcomes for patients with advanced MCC. Current US Food and Drug Administration-approved ICIs in this setting include the PD-L1 inhibitor avelumab and PD-1 inhibitors pembrolizumab and retifanlimab. In this podcast, we summarize key studies of ICIs in advanced MCC, including clinical trials and real-world studies, and discuss clinical evidence related to practical considerations, such as elective discontinuation of ICI treatment, and treatment of patients with immunocompromised or immunosuppressed status. We also discuss initial findings from studies of ICI-based combinations in patients with advanced MCC and ICI treatment in earlier stages of MCC, and highlight the emerging role of circulating tumor DNA for predicting disease recurrence. Overall, these developments demonstrate the positive impact of ICIs in the treatment of MCC and illustrate ongoing efforts to further improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Spondin 1 Enriched in p16Ink4a Reporter-Labeled Fibroblasts Promotes Melanoma Cell Proliferation in Vitro and Is Associated with Poor Prognosis.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment contains phenotypically diverse stromal cells that can support tumor progression; however, the identity and function of stromal populations expressing the senescence marker p16Ink4a in melanoma remain poorly defined. We combined p16-CreERT2-tdTomato lineage tracing with single-cell RNA sequencing in a syngeneic YUMMER1.7-H2B-GFP5 melanoma model to characterize p16Ink4a-lineage-positive [p16-Lin(+)] stromal cells and identify candidate mediators of tumor-stroma interactions. Immunofluorescence detected p16-Lin(+) cells across multiple stromal populations, while transcriptomic analysis identified fibroblasts as a major p16-Lin(+) stromal population. The integration of differentially expressed genes in p16-Lin(+) fibroblasts with a secretome database and survival data from The Cancer Genome Atlas Skin Cutaneous Melanoma cohort identified spondin 1 (SPON1) as a candidate extracellular mediator. Spon1 was preferentially expressed in fibroblasts, upregulated in the p16-Lin(+) fraction, and nearly undetectable in YUMMER1.7-H2B-GFP5 cells. Immobilized recombinant SPON1 promoted YUMM1.7 cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner in vitro. In an independent human skin tumor single-cell dataset, SPON1 expression was enriched in fibroblasts, with higher enrichment observed in those expressing CDKN2A, which encodes p16INK4A. Moreover, high SPON1 expression was independently associated with shorter overall survival after adjusting for tumor type, age, and sex. Together, these findings identify SPON1 as a candidate factor enriched in p16-Lin(+) fibroblasts, with potential functional and prognostic relevance in melanoma.

papers.title: Association between genotype and long-term risk of reintervention and distant metastases in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1-associated duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors are the leading cause of mortality in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, due to distant metastasis. Although surgery is the cornerstone of management, patients may require reintervention for disease progression or hormone-related morbidity. The clinical and genetic determinants of reintervention and long-term oncologic outcomes after index duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor surgery in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 remain unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients with genetically confirmed multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 and duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors evaluated at our institution from 1985 to 2024. Reintervention was defined as any subsequent surgical or locoregional therapy. Kaplan-Meier methods and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate predictors of reintervention-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival, focusing on truncating versus nontruncating MEN1 variants. Among 153 patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, 94 (61%) underwent surgical resection for duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors at a median age of 40 (interquartile range, 28-49) years. After a median follow-up of 16.4 years, 25 patients (27%) required reintervention, with 45 total procedures performed. Truncating multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 variants were significantly more common among patients undergoing reintervention (88.0% vs 63.8%; P = .024). On multivariable analysis, truncating genotype was independently associated with reintervention (hazard ratio, 3.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.25-16.68; P = .036). Among 84 patients without metastases at surgery, 24 (28.6%) developed distant metastases during follow-up; truncating genotype independently predicted shorter distant metastasis-free survival (hazard ratio, 5.55; 95% confidence interval, 1.56-35.40; P = .024). Notably, 37.5% of patients who developed metastases had a largest resected tumor ≤2 cm. Over a quarter of patients undergoing surgery for multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1-associated duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors require reintervention for progressive disease, and truncating MEN1 variants confer a nearly 4-fold higher risk of reintervention and >5-fold higher risk of distant metastatic progression during follow-up. Our findings underscore the limitations of size-based surgical algorithms and suggest that germline genotype may provide complementary prognostic information to refine postoperative risk stratification and surveillance strategies.

papers.title: IL7R mRNA therapy enhances antitumor T cell immunity and suppresses tumor growth in preclinical tumor models.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-7 receptor (IL7R) signaling is critical for T-cell survival, homeostasis, and immune function, but the therapeutic potential of increasing IL7R expression through messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery remains poorly defined. We investigated whether IL7R mRNA therapy could enhance antitumor immunity and improve tumor control in preclinical cancer models. IL7R mRNA formulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) was administered by combined intratumoral and intravenous injection in syngeneic B16 melanoma and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, with empty LNPs included as vehicle controls. Therapeutic efficacy, IL7R expression, immune responses, transcriptomic remodeling, T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire changes, and treatment tolerability were evaluated using complementary molecular, immunological, and sequencing approaches. IL7R mRNA treatment increased IL7R transcript and protein levels in tumor-bearing mice, whereas empty LNPs did not produce comparable increases. Treatment increased tumor-infiltrating CD8 T-cell frequencies, suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in both B16 and LLC models; empty LNP controls did not reproduce the therapeutic effect. Cytokine and transcriptomic analyses showed treatment-associated activation of inflammatory, T-cell, interferon, and antigen-receptor signaling programs. TCR sequencing further demonstrated increased repertoire diversity and reduced clonal dominance following IL7R mRNA treatment. No obvious body-weight loss or marked changes in serum alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, or creatinine were observed under the tested conditions. IL7R mRNA therapy increases IL7R expression and is associated with enhanced T-cell antitumor responses, tumor growth suppression, improved survival, and remodeling of the tumor immune environment. These findings support further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation of IL7R mRNA-based cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Size Under Scrutiny: Preoperative Imaging Size of Mesenteric Deposits Does Not Predict Oncological Outcomes in Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSmall intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SiNETs) are rare tumors with propensity to cause bulky fibrotic mesenteric masses by hematogenous and lymphatic invasion. They exhibit variable oncological behavior and reliable prognostic markers remain elusive. The 8th edition American Joint Commission on Cancer introduced mesenteric mass ≥2 cm to improve prognostication. The clinical utility in prognostication remains unknown. We reviewed outcomes of resected SiNETs to determine if computed tomography (CT) size is associated with oncological outcomes.MethodsRetrospective review of resected SiNET patients at two tertiary centers with evaluable preoperative CT scans. Measured the largest diameter of the mesenteric mass and the cutoff of 2 cm used to correlate with oncological outcomes.ResultsSeventy-three patients operated for SiNET with preoperative CT were included. The largest mesenteric mass was <2 cm in 28 and ≥2 cm in 45 patients. Cohorts were similar in demographic and clinical characteristics. Median follow-up was 47 months. Overall survival (OS) and progression free survival (PFS) were similar. No significant differences in estimated mean OS (136 vs 139 months, P = 0.981) or median PFS (90 vs 71 months, P = 0.126) for the <2 cm and >2 cm cohorts, respectively. Univariable analysis failed to show an association between mesenteric size as a continuous variable, and at the ≥2 cmcutoff. Age, cardiac comorbidities, and palliative intent surgery were the only factors that correlated with survival.DiscussionMesenteric mass size on preoperative CT was not correlated with oncological outcomes and by itself showed little utility in preoperative decision-making.

papers.title: An Unexpected Finding in a Small Duodenal Subepithelial Lesion.
Outcomes after first recurrence of Merkel cell carcinoma: A retrospective cohort of 159 patients.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is an aggressive skin cancer with a recurrence rate of 40%. Data on outcomes after a first recurrence remains scarce. To evaluate survival and prognostic factors after a first recurrence of MCC. We analyzed patients from a historical-prospective cohort (1998-2023) who developed recurrence after completion of treatment for stage I-III disease. The primary endpoint was disease-specific survival (DSS) after first recurrence. Secondary objectives included identification of prognostic factors for MCC-related death after first recurrence. Among 383 stage I-III patients, 159 (41.5%) recurred. Median DSS after first recurrence was 18.3 months (95% CI 12.8-75.3). Among patients receiving systemic therapy at recurrence, median DSS was shorter in those receiving chemotherapy/targeted therapy vs immunotherapy (10.4 months vs not reached, p = 0.015). In multivariable analysis, immunosuppression (hazard ratio (HR) 2.69) and early recurrence (<6 months) (HR 1.92) were associated with increased mortality, while locoregional recurrence (HR 0.45) and radiotherapy administered at recurrence (HR 0.45) were associated with a reduced risk of death. Absence of systemic treatment at first recurrence was associated with a significantly higher risk of death compared with ICI therapy (HR 3.04). Retrospective design, low rates of sentinel lymph node biopsy procedures, heterogeneity of therapeutic regimens over two decades. Immunosuppression, early recurrence, and distant recurrence are associated with poor prognosis after first recurrence of MCC, whereas radiotherapy administered at recurrence is associated with improved survival. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors did not retain an independent prognostic impact in multivariable analysis, univariate findings suggest a potential survival benefit in selected patients receiving systemic therapy.

papers.title: DNA nanodevice-engineered macrophages as living sensors for dual-mode in vivo monitoring of tumor-associated macrophage polarization.
papers.abstract: Exploiting macrophages as cell-autonomous reporters of their polarization states represents a promising strategy for interrogating tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) phenotypes in cancer. Here, we develop a macrophage-based sensing platform, termed eMφ. This platform is created by engineering macrophages with a modular and multiplexable DNA origami nanodevice to report TAM polarization states within the tumor microenvironment. Upon tumor infiltration, microenvironmental cues drive macrophage polarization, triggering the engineered system to convert endogenous signals (e.g., Arg1 or iNOS mRNA) into distinct, state-specific reporter outputs. The integration of local and circulating reporters enables compartment-resolved, multiscale readouts of macrophage state. Following intravenous administration, eMφ facilitates tumor detection across multiple murine models, including B16F10 melanoma and lung metastasis, and enables precise evaluation of macrophage-reprogramming immunotherapy. Overall, this work establishes DNA nanodevice-programmed macrophages as a novel class of synthetic-living hybrid systems, paving the way for programmable and precise immune-state diagnostics and therapy.

papers.title: Aberrant Desmin Expression in a Middle Ear Neuroendocrine Tumor: Expanding the Immunophenotypic Spectrum.
papers.abstract: Middle ear neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are uncommon neoplasms that exhibit both epithelial and neuroendocrine differentiation. Aberrant desmin expression in middle ear NET has not been documented previously and may create a diagnostic pitfall due to morphologic overlap with myogenic and rhabdoid tumors. A 52-year-old man presented with right ear pain, fullness, and facial deviation. Imaging revealed a soft-tissue mass involving the middle ear cavity and the mastoid air cells, with ossicular erosion. Histopathology showed an infiltrative neoplasm arranged in nests, trabeculae, cords, and pseudoacini composed of monomorphic cells with plasmacytoid/rhabdoid morphology. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells showed diffuse positivity for KRT, synaptophysin, chromogranin, and diffuse strong desmin expression, while myogenin, MYOD1, p63, calponin, TTF1, CDX2, and GATA3 were negative. SMARCB1/INI1 expression was retained, and the Ki67 index was <2%. A diagnosis of middle ear NET with aberrant desmin positivity was rendered. The patient remained disease-free 18 months following surgical excision. The index patient expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of middle ear NET by documenting diffuse aberrant desmin expression. Awareness of this unusual finding is important to avoid misdiagnosis as rhabdomyosarcoma or other rhabdoid neoplasms. Accurate diagnosis requires careful integration of morphologic and immunohistochemical features, and long-term follow-up remains essential despite the generally indolent behavior of middle ear NETs.

papers.title: Retifanlimab Versus Avelumab for the Treatment of Metastatic Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Analysis.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and aggressive skin cancer with poor prognosis and low survival rate. Retifanlimab and avelumab are monoclonal immune checkpoint inhibitor antibodies approved for metastatic or recurrent locally advanced MCC. The objective of this study was to analyze clinical outcomes with retifanlimab versus avelumab using a matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC). Individual patient data from the phase 2 POD1UM-201 trial (NCT03599713, data cutoff July 2024) were used for the retifanlimab treatment group, and aggregate data from part B of the phase 2 JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial (NCT02155647) were used for the avelumab treatment group. Key prognostic factors/effect modifiers identified from published literature (age, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, programmed cell death ligand 1 status, and disease characteristics) were selected for adjustment in the base case. Scenario analyses were also conducted, including additional covariates. An unanchored MAIC was conducted for overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall response rate (ORR). After weighing characteristics, the effective sample size of the adjusted retifanlimab population was approximately 42 patients (47% of original sample size). In the base case analysis, weighted hazard ratio (95% CI) numerically favored retifanlimab versus avelumab for OS (0.800 [0.492, 1.303]) and was statistically significant for PFS (0.590 [0.396, 0.881]), with the latter driven by separation during the first 2 months of treatment. Weighted odds ratio numerically favored retifanlimab for ORR (1.871 [0.896, 3.908)]. Scenario analyses generally confirmed base case analyses. Results of this MAIC generally favored retifanlimab compared with avelumab, including a statistically significant difference in PFS and numerical trends in OS and ORR, building on the clinical evidence supporting retifanlimab for the treatment of metastatic MCC. These findings are subject to residual confounding and should be interpreted with caution.

papers.title: Activator of Sirt6 exerts antitumor activity in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) is one of the most common intracranial neuroendocrine tumors. Surgical resection is the first choice for most subtypes of PitNETs. However, radical removal of invasive tumors remains challenging. A novel pharmacological therapy is objectively needed. Sirtuin 6 (Sirt6) is a member of the NAD+-dependent class III deacetylase sirtuin family, which plays a key role in tumorigenesis in many tumors. However, the role of Sirt6 and its activator in PitNETs is still unclear. In the study, we investigated the expression of Sirt6 and the antitumor effect of the Sirt6 activator MDL-800 in PitNETs. The expression of Sirt6 was detected in PitNET and cell lines by RNA-seq, immunohistochemistry, and western blotting. To test Sirt6 and its activator MDL-800, the cell viability, clone formation, and xenograft experiment were conducted. Autophagy was evaluated by microscopy and western blotting analysis. The efficacy of MDL-800 in the human primary PitNET cells was also investigated by the cell viability assay. Low expression of Sirt6 was found in PitNET tissues and two pituitary cell lines. Sirt6 inhibited cell proliferation and clone formation. Treatment with MDL-800 suppressed cell growth in vitro and in vivo. Further mechanistic studies showed that MDL-800 could lead to lethal autophagy and exert an antitumor effect in human primary PitNET cells. Our results suggest that activation of Sirt6 by its selective activator MDL-800 is a promising therapy for PitNETs.

papers.title: A post-operative fluid restriction protocol reduces the incidence of delayed hyponatremia following trans-sphenoidal pituitary surgery.
papers.abstract: The study assessed the effect of a postoperative fluid restriction on the incidence of delayed hyponatremia (DH) following transsphenoidal pituitary surgery (TSS). The incidence of DH in the prospective cohort was compared to that of a published retrospective cohort from our centre managed according to the standard postoperative protocol without fluid restriction. This prospective interventional study included patients aged ≥18 years who underwent TSS for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). A structured postoperative fluid restriction of ≤1.5 L/day was implemented from post-operative day 5 (POD5) to POD14, with daily intake/output monitoring. Serum sodium was measured at defined postoperative intervals. DH incidence in the prospective cohort was compared with a previously published retrospective cohort managed without fluid restriction. Patient adherence and satisfaction were assessed using a study-specific questionnaire. The study included 78 patients with a mean(SD) age of 42.6(11.9) years. Seventy-two (92.3%) patients had macroadenomas and 35.9% of the tumors were invasive. Twelve (15.4%) patients developed early transient AVP deficiency. Eleven (14.1%) patients developed DH between POD 5-14, compared to 36% in the retrospective cohort (p = 0.001). None in the prospective cohort required readmission or prolonged hospitalization for hyponatremia and the hyponatremia resolved with further tighter fluid restriction. Seven patients developed mild asymptomatic hypernatremia/increased serum osmolarity which resolved with relaxation of fluid intake. A structured fluid restriction protocol of ≤1.5 L/day in the post-operative period may be safe and effective in reducing the incidence of delayed hyponatremia and readmissions following transsphenoidal pituitary surgery for PitNETs in a tropical setting.

papers.title: Paraganglioma of the Lumbar Spine: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, with spinal involvement representing a small minority of cases. Lumbar spinal paragangliomas are especially uncommon and may present with nonspecific symptoms, often mimicking more common intradural tumors. We describe a 49-year-old female who presented with chronic low back and sacral pain, along with bilateral lower extremity symptoms. Lumbar MRI demonstrated an intrathecal, homogeneously enhancing mass at L3 causing canal stenosis. The patient underwent lumbar laminectomy with gross total resection of an intradural, extramedullary lesion. Histopathology confirmed a paraganglioma, with immunohistochemical positivity for chromogranin A, synaptophysin, and S100. Postoperatively, she reported substantial relief of pain and radiculopathy, with no neurological deficits. Surveillance MRI at seven weeks and 4.5 months showed no residual or recurrent tumor. Although rare, lumbar paragangliomas should be considered in the differential diagnosis of intradural, extramedullary masses. Gross total surgical resection offers effective symptom relief and favorable short-term outcomes. Given the potential for delayed recurrence, we recommend close postoperative surveillance with MRI every three to six months during the initial follow-up period.

papers.title: Pediatric Paraganglioma Presenting with Spinal Cord Edema.
Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Clinical and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) are a heterogeneous group of malignancies characterized by the expression of neuroendocrine markers. In recent years, GEP-NENs have gained increasing clinical attention because of their rising prevalence and the need for more effective therapeutic strategies for them. GEP-NENs are classified into gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) and gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas (GEP-NECs), based on the Ki-67 proliferation index and histological differentiation. GEP-NETs are generally characterized by relatively indolent clinical behavior, typically limited genomic alterations, and responsiveness to molecularly targeted therapies, whereas GEP-NECs are highly aggressive neoplasms frequently harboring TP53 and RB1 alterations, and are typically treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy. Though these definitions provide a useful framework for tumor classification, real-world GEP-NENs frequently exhibit substantial intra- and intertumoral heterogeneity, making clinical interpretation considerably more complex. Recently, a subset of well-differentiated neoplasms with high Ki-67 indices has been recognized as gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors G3 (GEP-NETG3), representing tumors that do not fit neatly into the conventional classification system. Treatment strategy for GEP-NETG3 highlights the difficulties faced for filling the gap between pathological classification and biomarkers currently used to guide clinical management. Addressing this challenge requires a multifaceted approach, integrating clinical and translational research to better capture the biological complexity of these tumors. In this review, we summarize the current understanding of GEP-NENs, focusing on their biological features, therapeutic implications, and emerging insights from both clinical and translational research perspectives.

papers.title: The CGRP-nociceptor axis in cancer: tumor-specific programs of immune evasion, stromal remodeling, and tumor growth.
papers.abstract: Cancer neuroscience has established that peripheral nerves can shape tumor growth and antitumor immunity, although the underlying mechanisms vary across malignancies. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), released mainly by peptidergic nociceptors and sensed through the CALCRL/RAMP1 receptor complex, is emerging as a recurrent mediator of tumor-nerve communication. This review synthesizes current evidence for CGRP signaling across tumor types. In melanoma and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), CGRP can directly suppress tumor-infiltrating T cell activity. In lung adenocarcinoma, it acts through a macrophage-fibroblast relay that limits tertiary lymphoid structure assembly. In medullary thyroid cancer, tumor-associated CGRP is linked to abnormal dendritic cell development. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, nociceptor-derived CGRP participates in a reciprocal interaction with cancer-associated fibroblasts that lowers IL-15 and suppresses natural killer cells. Additional studies identify tumor-intrinsic outputs, including gastric tumor growth, CGRP-dependent cytoprotective autophagy in oral cancer, and RAMP1-dependent growth in gastrointestinal cancer models. Liver data currently support a role in fibrogenesis, while the relevance of this pathway to hepatocellular carcinoma remains unresolved. Together, these findings support a shared nociceptor-CGRP signaling system with tumor-specific cellular outputs. CGRP-pathway drugs and nociceptor-directed interventions therefore warrant tumor-specific translational studies, although anticancer efficacy remains predominantly preclinical.

papers.title: Immunohistochemical profiling of PD-L1 expression in neuroendocrine carcinoma of the uterine cervix.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) of the uterine cervix is a rare and aggressive malignancy for which disease-specific treatment strategies remain limited. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have demonstrated activity in several cancers, PD-L1 expression in cervical NEC remains insufficiently characterized. This study descriptively evaluated PD-L1 expression patterns in cervical NEC using the PD-L1 IHC 22C3 pharmDx assay. Six surgically resected cervical NEC specimens from Taiwanese women treated between 2010 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. PD-L1 expression was assessed using the PD-L1 IHC 22C3 pharmDx assay. TPS, CPS, and IC scores were evaluated descriptively; TC was also recorded but was numerically identical to TPS in all cases and is therefore reported jointly as TPS/TC. Thresholds of TPS/TC ≥1%, CPS ≥1, and IC ≥5% were used solely for exploratory analyses and were not interpreted as validated clinical cutoffs for cervical NEC. Tumor-cell PD-L1 expression was uncommon, with TPS/TC ≥1% observed in one case (16.7%). CPS ≥1 and IC ≥5% were each observed in three of six cases (50%). PD-L1 staining was more frequently observed in tumor-infiltrating immune cells than in tumor cells. One case demonstrated dual-compartment staining, with CPS 25, TPS/TC 3%, and IC 30%. In this small cohort, PD-L1 expression was heterogeneous. Tumor-cell positivity by TPS/TC was uncommon and largely limited to a single case, whereas PD-L1 staining was more frequently observed in immune cells. CPS and IC provided complementary descriptive information on PD-L1 distribution; however, their biological relevance and predictive value remain unvalidated in cervical NEC. Larger studies integrating molecular profiling, functional immune characterization, and clinical outcome data are needed to determine the potential clinical utility of PD-L1 assessment in this rare malignancy.

papers.title: Conversion therapy followed by curative resection in a patient with ACTH-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor G3: a case report.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNETs) with ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) production are uncommon, highly aggressive, and carry a dismal prognosis. Early nonspecific symptoms often delay diagnosis, and treatment strategies remain controversial. For patients with locally advanced pNETs, conversion therapy has only rarely been reported and remains a sparingly applied strategy. A 37-year-old woman presented with a six-month history of progressive swelling in both lower extremities and her face. Further workup confirmed ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome. CT and MRI identified a 5.7 × 2.8 cm lesion in the pancreatic body/tail that invaded the left adrenal gland and splenic vessels, accompanied by retroperitoneal lymph node spread. Biopsy results indicated a G3 pNET. Given the borderline resectable status due to local advancement, she received conversion therapy comprising a long-acting somatostatin analogue followed by CapTem chemotherapy. After three months of neoadjuvant treatment, imaging showed modest primary tumor shrinkage and marked reduction of lymph node size, reflecting successful downstaging. Subsequently, she underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy, left adrenalectomy, and lymph node dissection, achieving R0 resection. Final pathology confirmed a G3 pNET (Ki-67 30%-40%) with positive SSTR2 and ACTH immunostaining. Although the patient eventually experienced disease progression and succumbed to COVID-19 infection 37 months after initial diagnosis, this case illustrates that conversion therapy can render an initially borderline resectable high-grade pNET amenable to curative resection. This report underscores the aggressive trajectory of ACTH-secreting pNET G3 and suggests the potential utility of conversion therapy. Further studies are needed to validate this approach.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and immunotherapy in Chinese patients with Merkel cell carcinoma: a retrospective analysis.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare but highly aggressive cutaneous malignancy with limited epidemiological and therapeutic data in Asian populations. While immunotherapy works in Western patients, its efficacy in Chinese MCC patients remains unexplored. We retrospectively analyzed 40 histologically confirmed MCC cases treated at our institution between November 2011 to November 2024. Sixteen patients with complete records underwent detailed analysis of demographics, treatments, and responses. The cohort included 25 female and 15 male patients (median age 71 years, range 25-91). Of the 16 patients with detailed information, 15 (94%) patients underwent extensive resection while 1 did not. Among surgical patients, 1 (7%) patient operative area received postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy, and 2 (13%) had additional lymph node dissection. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that out of 10 evaluable patients, 8 (80%) were MCPyV positive and 3 (30%) were PD-L1 positive. Among the patients receiving systemic treatment, four were administered Pembrolizumab at a dose of 200 mg every three weeks. Remarkably, three of these patients (75%) achieved a complete response (CR) by radiographic evaluation, with two of the treated specimens showed no residual malignant cells detected in post-treatment biopsy specimens. The treatment was well-tolerated, with no grade 3 or higher adverse events reported during the observation period. This study describes MCC characteristics in Chinese patients, with preliminary indications of female predominance and favorable immunotherapy responses. The findings highlight the need for standardized treatment approaches.

papers.title: Establishing a Routine Teleconsultation Follow-Up Clinic in a Tertiary Care Hospital of a Low-Middle-Income Country: An Operational Blueprint and Implementation Experience.
papers.abstract: Literature on teleconsultation is rich in outcome data, and only a smaller body of work has described the operational setup of specific teleconsultation services, mainly from the COVID-era. However, publications on a routine, non-pandemic, low-cost, and asynchronous departmental teleconsultation model built on a widely available messaging application remain scarce. No structured replicable blueprint exists for establishing such a model for follow-up clinics at the departmental level in a government tertiary care hospital. We describe a step-by-step operational framework implemented in the Department of Endocrine and Breast Surgery since May 2025, which has now served 587 teleconsultations (post-thyroidectomy, post-parathyroidectomy, breast carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma) over 13 months. The model requires no dedicated funding, no institutional IT infrastructure, and no proprietary telemedicine platform. It uses a dedicated departmental smartphone, WhatsApp, a structured asynchronous review schedule, and a documentation proforma aligned with India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) Telemedicine Practice Guidelines, 2020. WhatsApp was selected over e-Sanjeevani for its asynchronous capability, universal patient accessibility, and zero registration burden. The average clinician time per teleconsultation is 5-10 minutes; the entire daily review session is completed within 30 minutes. The underlying principles are specialty-agnostic and potentially adaptable to cardiology, neurology, hematology, and oncology, though each specialty would require its own eligibility criteria and escalation thresholds.

papers.title: Same-day diagnosis and robotic resection of rare primary pulmonary melanoma: a robotic bronchoscopy-guided approach.
papers.abstract: This case report describes a rare presentation of pulmonary melanoma of unknown primary managed through a same-day robotic diagnostic and therapeutic approach. A man in his 70s with an incidentally detected lingular pulmonary nodule suspicious for non-small cell lung cancer underwent robotic navigation bronchoscopy for biopsy and dye marking, immediately followed by robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Intraoperative frozen section revealed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, prompting definitive surgical resection during the same anaesthetic event. Final histopathology and molecular analysis confirmed melanoma, with no identifiable cutaneous, mucosal or ocular primary. The patient subsequently received adjuvant immunotherapy and remains disease-free at 24 months. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of pulmonary melanoma mimicking lung carcinoma and demonstrates how integration of robotic bronchoscopy and robotic surgery can enable rapid diagnosis, definitive management and streamlined care within a single operative session.

papers.title: SERS sensing platform based on MIL-100(Fe)@AgNPs for norepinephrine/adenosine monitoring in patient plasma.
papers.abstract: The excessive activation of sympathetic nerve is closely related to cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In this study, we developed a novel MIL-100(Fe)@Ag surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate for the simultaneous and effective detection of plasma norepinephrine (NE) and adenosine-two pivotal sympathetic hormones. The microscopic morphology and crystal structure of the substrate were characterized using techniques such as transmission electron microscope (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mechanistically, the HOMO-LUMO energy levels of the detection molecules were calculated using Gaussian. The substrate realized a dual SERS enhancement mechanism through the synergistic effect of localized surface plasmon resonance and interfacial charge transfer. Consequently, the MIL-100(Fe)@Ag platform exhibited high-sensitivity quantitative detection capabilities for NE and adenosine: the detection limit for NE is 0.596 nmol/L; the detection limit for adenosine is 0.24 nmol/L. Crucially, when applied to patients with pheochromocytoma-a neuroendocrine tumor characterized by plasma catecholamine surges, this method achieved robust and stable detection of plasma NE. It offered comparable diagnostic accuracy to conventional mass spectrometry while significantly reducing analysis complexity. Therefore, this innovative strategy may hold great promise for the long-term, decentralized monitoring of sympathetic nerve activity in populations at risk for CVDs or related clinical disorders.

papers.title: Correction: Co-delivery of doxorubicin and siRNA using octreotide-conjugated gold nanorods for targeted neuroendocrine cancer therapy.
papers.abstract: Correction for 'Co-delivery of doxorubicin and siRNA using octreotide-conjugated gold nanorods for targeted neuroendocrine cancer therapy' by Yuling Xiao et al., Nanoscale, 2012, 4, 7185-7193, https://doi.org/10.1039/C2NR31853A.

papers.title: Alternative lengthening of telomeres in small well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: independent validation and cross-platform concordance.
papers.abstract: Well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors measuring ≤ 2 cm (small PanNETs) are usually non-functional and most are discovered incidentally. While most are indolent, some behave aggressively and metastasize. Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) has shown promise as a predictive biomarker of recurrence in recent studies. We designed a multi-institutional study to validate the predictive ability of ALT in small PanNET to inform patient selection for operative versus non-operative management. We identified 172 cases of small PanNET diagnosed from 2001 to 2021 in four different institutions. ALT fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) could be performed in 133 cases and was compared with clinical outcomes. Among those with FISH, 44.4% were females with a mean age of 65.4 years (range 31-88). Twenty-one cases (15.8%) were ALT-positive. Over a median follow-up of 48 months, a total of 19 progressions (metastasis, recurrence, increase in size, or death) were recorded. ALT positivity was significantly associated with worse progression-free survival [PFS]. In the ALT-positive group, a total of 9 cases showed progression compared to 10 in the ALT-negative group (5-year PFS: 70.2% vs. 88.8%, hazard ratio: 4.69, p = 0.002). In a separate analysis using matched cases, ALT chromogenic in situ hybridization (CISH), demonstrated high concordance with ALT FISH (95.5% for positive and 91.7% for negative cases) enabling cross-platform validation. Unlike FISH, CISH can be interpreted using standard bright field microscopy, facilitating broader implementation. These findings support further evaluation of ALT testing, particularly via CISH, as a potentially scalable and accessible biomarker, while recognizing that formal analytic validation and confirmation in unselected cohorts are required before routine clinical implementation.

papers.title: VEGF pathway signalling across pulmonary neuroendocrine tumours: associations with histological subtypes in a multicentre study.
papers.abstract: The current classification of pulmonary neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) is primarily based on histomorphological criteria, which do not fully capture their underlying biological heterogeneity. This limitation is particularly evident among pulmonary carcinoids, a subgroup characterized by highly variable clinical behaviour and prognostic outcomes despite similar morphological features.Angiogenesis is a hallmark of NENs, yet the role of the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) pathway in pulmonary NENs remains incompletely defined.In this multicentre retrospective study, 109 pulmonary NENs (67 typical carcinoids, 22 atypical carcinoids, and 20 high-grade NENs) were analysed. VEGF, VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry and correlated with clinicopathological features and outcome.VEGF pathway components showed subtype-specific expression patterns. VEGFR1 was reduced in high-grade tumours and displayed a bimodal distribution, while VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 were higher in atypical carcinoids and high-grade tumours. Survival and recurrence were driven by histological subtype, whereas VEGF pathway expression lacked independent prognostic significance.The higher expression of VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 observed in atypical carcinoids and high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas suggests a possible involvement of the VEGF signalling pathway in tumour biology. These findings contribute to the biological characterization of pulmonary NENs and provide a rationale for future studies investigating whether VEGF pathway markers may have predictive relevance for anti-angiogenic therapies.

papers.title: Ki-67 antigen in lung carcinoids/neuroendocrine tumors: from a proliferation marker to a clinical compass.
papers.abstract: Ki-67 has extensively been studied in lung neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), including typical and atypical carcinoid, yet it has never been formally accepted into classification. Its clinical application was limited to the differential diagnosis toward neuroendocrine carcinomas and the characterization of carcinoids with increased proliferation rates. Recently, the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) has released a novel grading-based classification, in which Ki-67 pays a central and decisional role. This review examines the role of Ki-67 in lung NETs from three complementary perspectives (available English literature in PubMed, National Library of Medicine): (i) methodological issues, specimen types, grading-based classification, and molecular correlations; (ii) impact of statistical methods on study findings; (iii) clinical implications of a grading-based classification for diagnostic phase, hereditary syndromes, and therapeutic decision-making. The proposed grading-driven classification is likely to reshape established concepts and practices in the field of lung NETs, in future classifications. An awareness of the strengths and limitations of statistical methods used to define the distribution and significance of Ki-67 is essential for generating reliable, reproducible, and clinically meaningful evidence.

papers.title: Hemorrhagic pancreatic schwannoma mimicking a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
Development of dual SST2/SST5 targeting radioligands through rational structural design.
papers.abstract: Radioligand therapy targeting somatostatin receptors has emerged as a highly effective treatment strategy for neuroendocrine tumors, with growing evidence indicating that SST2 antagonists and dual SST2/SST5 targeting approaches may further enhance tumor coverage and therapeutic efficacy. In this study, DOTA-NOC, a somatostatin analog with high affinity for SST2 and SST5, served as the scaffold for the design of novel ligands incorporating structural features associated with receptor antagonism. The resulting ligands were conjugated to DOTA for 177Lu radiolabeling and evaluated for receptor affinity, antagonistic potency, and in vivo properties. Among the series, 177Lu-10 displayed high affinity for both receptor subtypes while acting selectively as an SST5 antagonist. Compared to [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-NOC, it showed similar SST2 tumor uptake but nearly 5-fold higher accumulation in SST5-expressing tumors. This work provides new insights into the structural determinants underlying SST2 and SST5 affinity, selectivity, and antagonistic behavior, demonstrating that receptor recognition and functional activity arise from the combined contribution of multiple structural elements and supporting the development of dual SST2/SST5-targeted radioligands.

papers.title: Merkel cell carcinoma in a patient on ruxolitinib treatment for polycythemia vera.
Reirradiation of recurrent brain tumors: a review by the ESTRO CNS Focus Group.
papers.abstract: Reirradiation has become an area of increasing clinical and scientific interest, particularly in neuro-oncology. This non-systematic review on central nervous system (CNS) tumors by the CNS focus group of the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology provides a pragmatic synthesis of the available evidence, excluding gliomas. We address key questions related to patient selection, fractionation, technical considerations, and treatment safety. Relevant studies on the use of reirradiation for meningiomas, ependymomas, brain metastases, and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, as well as on the management of radiation necrosis, have been reviewed and summarized. Reirradiation has been used with varying success in primary and secondary brain tumors. The appropriate use of reirradiation requires consideration of numerous factors, including, but not limited to, prior treatment courses, fractionation, dose to organs at risk, imaging findings, the volume of the recurrent tumor, and the interval since prior treatments. The vast majority of available studies are limited by their retrospective design, lack of standardization in reporting, and overall heterogeneity across cohorts and treatments. Several reirradiation studies across different tumor entities suggest potential efficacy and safety in carefully selected patients. However, important limitations remain, underscoring the need for well-designed prospective studies with rigorous reporting in both primary and secondary brain tumors.

papers.title: Insulin-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor presenting with hypoglycemia in a patient with a paternally inherited ABCC8 variant: a case report and literature review.
Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor PET/CT in gastrinomas: a case series demonstrating the precise characterization to guide surgical and medical treatment.
papers.abstract: Gastrinoma is a rare type of neuroendocrine tumor with ectopic secretion of gastrin causing Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (ZES). Accurate localization of gastrinomas and their metastases is important for developing precise treatment strategies. We reported three cases of metastatic gastrinomas evaluated with 68Ga-exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT. Despite most gastrinomas highly expressing somatostatin receptor (SSTR), these patients showed no or heterogeneous uptake on 68Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT, whereas 68Ga-exendin-4 PET/CT sensitively detected the primary tumor, lymph node metastasis, liver metastasis, and bone metastasis, facilitating accurate tumor assessment and supporting clinical decision-making. The findings were correlated with enhanced CT and MRI and confirmed the location of the hormone-related tumors. This highlights the potential utility of 68Ga-exendin-4 PET/CT as a promising imaging modality for evaluating gastrinomas with no or heterogeneous SSTR expression and guiding precise treatment strategies.

papers.title: ATR inhibition induces NF-κB-dependent immunogenicity in Merkel cell carcinoma independent of cGAS-STING.
papers.abstract: There is a major unmet need to develop therapies for patients whose tumors do not respond to PD-1 blockade. Inhibition of the ATR-mediated DNA replication checkpoint has been reported to augment antitumor immunity, although the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly in cGAS-STING-deficient tumors. Here, we investigated the effects of ATR inhibition (ATRi) on tumor immunogenicity in Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), an aggressive skin cancer commonly driven by Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV). Among 92 primary MCC tumors, Ki-67 positivity was observed in 50% of MCPyV-positive and 83% of MCPyV-negative tumor cells, suggesting reliance on ATR-mediated replication stress responses. Notably, MCC frequently exhibits cGAS-STING deficiency, especially in MCPyV-positive tumors. In representative MCPyV-positive and -negative MCC cell lines, ATRi enhanced cytotoxicity and, alone or combined with low-dose radiation, induced proinflammatory NF-κB transcriptional programs. These included increased expression of MHC class I, antigen-processing machinery, interleukins, chemokines, and interferon-related genes. ATRi also increased surface calreticulin exposure and subsequent phagocytosis by human monocyte-derived macrophages. These findings support ATRi-mediated immune reprogramming in MCC cells through an NF-κB signaling cascade, regardless of cGAS-STING functional status. These observations support clinical evaluation of ATR inhibitors in immunotherapy-refractory disease (NCT05947500) and suggest candidate biomarkers of therapeutic response.

papers.title: Poliosis predicts durable response to immune-checkpoint blockade in metastatic melanoma: a multicenter cohort study.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) improved survival outcomes for patients with metastatic melanoma. Yet up to 65% of patients experience primary resistance and nearly half of initial responders acquire resistance. The clinical utility of ICB is further tempered by frequent immune-related adverse events (irAEs), which increase in severity and frequency with prolonged treatment duration. Hence, a pivotal challenge is to identify clinically accessible markers to predict durable ICB responses. While prior reports indicate that the development of cutaneous irAEs may reflect robust antitumor immune responses, there is limited evidence linking specific types of cutaneous irAEs to clinical ICB benefit. In this retrospective multicenter study, we investigated a cohort of 741 patients diagnosed with non-resectable stage III/IV melanoma who were treated with ICB between April 2012 and August 2025. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment regimens and survival outcomes were collected within six German skin cancer centers. We stratified patients by the type of cutaneous AE into such with whitening of the body skin (vitiligo), hair (poliosis) or other cutaneous AE. Primary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and objective response rates (ORR). Among 741 eligible patients, 221 developed cutaneous irAE within the median follow-up period of 48 months. Thereof, we observed tumor recurrences in 17.2% of patients with poliosis, 57.7% of patients developing vitiligo and 60.0% of patients with other cutaneous irAE. In line, we detected a significantly enhanced ORR (93.1% vs 58.8% vs 38.8%, p<0.001), prolonged PFS (Not reached, NR, vs 31 months vs 9 months, p<0.001) and overall survival (NR vs NR vs 69 months, p<0.001) in poliosis patients. Critically, enhanced tumor control in poliosis patients was seen regardless of initial tumor burden, treatment duration or the presence of melanoma brain metastases. While other AE usually arise early on ICB start, poliosis was a late event that occurred at a median of 6 months. Our study identifies poliosis as a distinct and immunologically-informed marker linked to strong and durable ICB responses easily applicable in a routine clinical setting. Detection of poliosis may complement radiographic imaging for clinical decision-making on ICB treatment duration and early cessation and provides a window for translational investigations harnessing epitope-specific T-cell responses to melanoma antigens.

papers.title: Transcription Factor Immunohistochemistry Improves Diagnostic Accuracy and Reduces Immunonegative Misclassification in Nonfunctional Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Anterior pituitary hormone immunohistochemistry (IHC) for surgically resected nonfunctional pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (NF PitNET) underreports true rates of tumor lineage and biases toward immunonegative tumors. Here we compare our use of traditional IHC methods for identification of anterior pituitary hormones versus identification of lineage specific transcription factors (TF) to correctly identify NF PitNET lineage and review the literature for studies evaluating its efficacy. A single institution, retrospective study of NF PitNETs undergoing surgical resection between 2021 and 2024 at the University of [blinded for review] was performed. Patients were included for study if pathology specimens had IHC performed for anterior pituitary hormones and lineage specific TF. A total of 173 patients with NF PitNETs were included. When stained for the lineage specific TFs: SF-1, PIT-1, and T-PIT, immunoreactivity was observed in 117 (66%), 18 (10%), and 35 (20%) tumors, respectively. Three (2%) patients demonstrated no positive staining for any TF and were classified as immunonegative. Of the 117 SF-1 tumors, 32 (27%) showed no positive staining for LH/FSH. For the 18 PIT-1 tumors, two (11%) showed no positive staining for PRL/GH/TSH. For the 35 TPIT tumors, 7 (20%) showed no staining for ACTH. Overall, of the 170 patients who had positive staining for a single TF, 41 (24%) did not show IHC staining for their corresponding anterior pituitary hormones and thus would have been classified as immunonegative PitNETs. Use of IHC for identification of lineage specific TF markedly improves the accuracy of correct pathological diagnosis of NF PitNETs.

papers.title: Accelerated Biological Aging and Risk of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Findings from a Large Prospective East Asian Cohort.
papers.abstract: The global increase in young-onset colorectal cancer (CRC, diagnosed before age 50) necessitates improved risk stratification. Biological age, which better reflects physiological deterioration than chronological age, may serve as a crucial indicator of disease susceptibility. We examined the association between accelerated biological aging and early-onset colorectal adenocarcinoma (EOCRC-AC) risk. In a prospective cohort of 198,491 Korean adults under 50 years of chronological age, we estimated biological age using Phenotypic Age (PhenoAge), derived from nine routine blood biomarkers, with acceleration calculated as the residual from regressing biological age on chronological age. Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for demographic, behavioral, and clinical factors, examined the association between biological age acceleration and incident EOCRC-AC, with colorectal neuroendocrine tumors (EOCRC-NET) analyzed as a comparator outcome. Over a median follow-up of 7.7 years, 127 incident EOCRC-AC and 142 EOCRC-NET were identified through linkage with the National Cancer Registry. Individuals with biological age greater than chronological age (accelerated biological aging) had a 93% higher risk of EOCRC-AC (hazard ratio [HR] 1.93, 95% CI 1.28-2.91), with particularly strong associations for colon adenocarcinoma (HR 2.32, 95% CI 1.38-3.89). Associations remained consistent across subgroups including adults younger than 45 years and lag-time sensitivity analyses. In contrast, no consistent association was observed for EOCRC-NET. Accelerated biological aging is independently associated with increased EOCRC-AC risk. Biological aging measures could complement chronological age-based criteria, improving risk stratification and identifying younger individuals who may benefit from earlier or tailored screening strategies.
